stories.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
stories.summary: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MVpi Roma artist Norbert Olah in the Bura Galeria in Budapest Image: Tobias Zuttmann/DW Advertisement The painting on the canvas is of a man playing chess with a robot. The color on his face is still damp and glistening. Norbert Olah was working into the early hours: The Bura Galeria in Budapest has been his studio all summer. He finds it easiest to concentrate at night, when the Hungarian capital gradually falls silent. Olah has taped foil and cardboard over the tiled floor at the back of the gallery. Pots of brushes, tubes of paint, pencil sketches, and, over and over again, pictures that include the blue-and-green Roma flag line the room. Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he deliberately left this part of his identity out of his art. Not because his ethnicity wasn't important to him, but because he didn't want to be labeled a "Romani artist." People in Ukraine are being killed every day by missiles, bombs, and drones . Now fisherfolk across Spain's Basque Country can no longer catch the animals, a prized delicacy at the center of what authorities describe as one of the world's most lucrative wildlife trafficking trades.
